description: This dataset comprises resting-state EEG recordings from 51 right-handed undergraduate participants, collected to investigate the relationship between resting-state EEG alpha/theta power, oscillatory dynamics, and trait anxiety. Participants completed a 4-minute alternating eyes-open and eyes-closed protocol while 256-channel EEG was recorded at 500 Hz. The dataset includes preprocessed EEG data and phenotypic measures of anxiety and personality traits, providing a resource for studying neural correlates of anxiety-related individual differences.
methods_description: EEG was recorded using a 256-channel EGI HydroCel Geodesic Sensor Net with Net Amps amplifier at 500 Hz sampling rate with online reference at Cz. The resting-state protocol consisted of alternating 1-minute eyes-open and eyes-closed blocks repeated twice. Preprocessing included bandpass filtering (0.1-50 Hz), line noise removal at 60 and 120 Hz, kurtosis-based channel rejection, re-referencing to average, ICA decomposition, and artifact component removal via ICLabel with visual inspection. Preprocessed data are provided in EEGLAB .set format. Phenotypic measures included the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Ten-Item Personality Inventory (TIPI) emotional stability subscale, and Behavioural Inhibition Scale/Fight-Flight-Freeze System (BIS/FFFS) from the RST-PQ.
